title: DIC and Survivors Pension: No Payment of Both for the Same Month
content:
**Product:** Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) for surviving spouses.

**Rule.** DIC and Survivors Pension are never paid to the same surviving spouse for the same month; a spouse entitled to both is paid the greater benefit unless they elect otherwise in writing, and the election is the spouse's own act.

### The rule in parts

| Element | What the rule says |
|---|---|
| Who | The same surviving spouse |
| What cannot happen | DIC and Survivors Pension paid for the same month |
| Default when entitled to both | The greater benefit is paid |
| Departure from the default | Only by the spouse's election otherwise, in writing |
| Whose act the election is | The spouse's own |

### Questions the rule answers

**A surviving spouse qualifies for both benefits and makes no election. What is paid?** The greater of the two benefits.

**Can VA staff make the election on the spouse's behalf, or accept it orally?** No. The election is the spouse's own act and is made in writing.

### Hypothetical illustration

A surviving spouse is entitled to both benefits, and for that spouse Survivors Pension would be the greater benefit. With no written election by the spouse, Survivors Pension, the greater benefit, is paid, and no DIC is paid for the same months. If the spouse elects DIC in writing, DIC is paid instead.
